- If sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- If sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) and prices are rising, model often underestimates; adjust upward to reflect momentum.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >70), model frequently overshoots in next few days; cap forecast at +5% above peak or use smoothing.
- When sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish mid-period, model often fails to reverse trend; apply mean reversion if sentiment drops below 0.33.
- If model forecast is flat or rising slowly while sentiment is volatile, consider downward bias; add 0.5–1.5% downward adjustment.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overestimates early in the period; apply 1–3% downward correction if sentiment is neutral or bearish.
- If sentiment history shows repeated 0.67–1.00 peaks, model tends to overreact; use sentiment-weighted smoothing to dampen overconfidence.
